transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-06-04T17:00:00Z
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Maya Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Ana Ruiz (BluePeak Head of ML), Ethan Cole (CTO), Priya Kapoor (PM), Luis Fernandez (Infra)

Summary: quick discovery focused on model selection tradeoffs for BluePeak's commerce chatbots and personalization APIs. Key themes: multilingual support, 32k+ context needs for session continuity, tool-calling (inventory/price checks), hosted vs dedicated latency/cost, and private/VPC constraints for EU data. Agreed next steps to exchange prompt corpus and run benchmarks.

Topics: model types (LLaMA/Mistral/RedPajama), context windows (8k/32k/100k), quantization impacts, function/tool calling reliability, caching (KV cache) and batching, private deployment network constraints, compliance (SOC2/data residency)

Transcript: 
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm samir from redwood, i'll kick us off. before we get into the model nitty-gritty, can we do quick intros?
[00:08] Ana: ana here, head of ML at bluepeak, we run the personalization engine for checkout and our chat assistant.
[00:12] Ethan: ethan, cto. we care about latency and cost.
[00:15] Priya: priya, pm for checkout assistant.
[00:18] Luis: luis infra. we manage cloud and compliance.
[00:21] Jordan: jordan, i'm the solutions engineer. we'll focus on model fit and infra tradeoffs today.
[00:26] Samir: cool. quick context from bluepeak side—what does throughput look like for chat? sessions per minute, average tokens per session?
[00:34] Ana: rough numbers, on peak we see ~1200 sessions per minute, average 220 tokens inbound and 600 tokens outbound across a 30–90 minute user session. also important is multi-turn: we need retention of prior user messages across 10–20 turns, sometimes with long product context, so larger context helpful.
[00:51] Jordan: ok that's great. so 600 outbound average, with 10-20 turns means effective context footprints get big, are you envisioning full history in the model or do you prefer summarization?
[01:02] Ana: ideally full-ish, but we can summarize older turns. for certain flows—returns, fraud review—we need full receipts/history for 30k tokens. so 32k context capability is a hard ask for some flows.
[01:15] Samir: noted. that pushes model selection toward long-context variants—there are hosted options with 32k and up, and dedicated/private deployments where we can bring 100k window models or run sliding window + KV cache.
[01:28] Priya: what's KV cache again? sorry, quick refresher.
[01:31] Jordan: KV cache is the key-value cache for transformer past-key-values; with session reuse we can avoid re-sending entire history every turn, especially for repeated prompts. helps latency and cost if you can reuse context server-side.
[01:41] Priya: okay makes sense.
[01:43] [00:41] Ethan: question on multilingual—our customers in EU and LATAM need Spanish and Portuguese at native-ish quality. are open models good enough or do we need mixing with LLM-as-a-service like openai?
[01:56] Jordan: good question. recent open models (Mistral, Mistral-instruct, Llama2 70B finetuned variants, RedPajama mixtures) vary. we typically see English-first models do worse in low-resource languages; some 30–70B multilingual derivatives perform reasonably. for high-quality Spanish/Portuguese we recommend either 1) a multilingual 32k model (hosted) with targeted finetuning or 2) a dedicated instance where you can run a larger quantized 70B or open-weights 100B variant for better coverage.
[02:22] Ana: hmm, we're sensitive to cost; can we quantize without losing too much Spanish fidelity?
[02:28] Jordan: yes, 4-bit and 8-bit quantization do well for many tasks but some subtle grammar and idiom handling degrade—we can run an eval on your Spanish corpus. we'll include evaluation metrics in the benchmark template.
[02:40] Samir: also worth noting our Optimize toolkit can suggest quantization profiles per workload to meet latency/cost targets.
[02:47] [03:00] Priya: tool-calling—this is critical: we need deterministic inventory lookups, price fetches, promo eligibility queries. how does redwood handle tool/function calling in production?
[03:12] Jordan: function-calling is supported both in hosted api and with dedicated. we expose structured outputs and a low-latency webhook/invoke path. for mission-critical calls we recommend separating inference for generation and a lightweight router to your internal inventory microservice. Redwood also has retry policies and fallback models for noisy outputs.
[03:30] Luis: are webhooks outbound from redwood or do we host a local connector in VPC? security folks prefer connectors in VPC to avoid egress.
[03:39] Jordan: for Private/VPC deployments we can run the connector inside the customer's VPC so no egress. Hosted mode uses secure outbound calls, but you can also use our dedicated with private networking for similar isolation.
[03:50] [04:10] Ethan: latency target is sub-200ms p50 for short completions, but for multi-turn personalized responses 300–450ms p50 is tolerable, p95 should be under 900ms. is that feasible on Dedicated?
[04:24] Jordan: yes on Dedicated with optimized batching and latency SLOs. Hosted can hit those numbers for smaller models and lighter throughput; with 1.2k sessions/minute peak you're in a range where Dedicated gives predictable tail latency and better cost.
[04:38] Samir: wanted to flag cost tradeoffs—hosting 32k models at scale is more expensive per token. Dedicated lets you amortize for heavy steady traffic. we'll put a cost model in the deck.
[04:51] [05:00] Ana: what's the rough delta? ballpark monthly for our traffic?
[05:04] Samir: we'll run numbers after you share sample traffic—i can give an example: hosted 32k variant might be X per token, Dedicated reserved capacity amortizes to Y per token after commit—we'll break it down in the spreadsheet.
[05:18] Priya: about model fidelity—how do we avoid hallucinations when we ask for inventory or price?
[05:24] Jordan: primary approach: structured tool calling and strict schema validation, secondary: prompt engineering with blocking/guardrails, and tertiary: deterministic retrieval augmentation—pass exact inventory snippets as context. also we can set up similarity-search embedding lookups to ground responses.
[05:41] Ana: retrieval augmentation—do you host the vector store or do we bring our own?
[05:45] Jordan: flexible. Hosted Redwood can host vector indexes, or you can point to your managed vector store (e.g., Pinecone/Weaviate) in Dedicated/Private. For GDPR constraints many customers host vectors in their VPC.
[05:58] [06:00] Priya: for a hybrid flow, we need to fallback to a smaller model when cost spikes. how easy is automatic fallback?
[06:08] Jordan: Redwood supports policy-based routing—route by latency budget, cost, or model health. automatic fallback can be to a cheaper quantized variant; we can also route to cached responses for known flows.
[06:18] Ana: ok and about A/B tests—can we run two models simultaneously for semantic parity tests?
[06:22] Samir: yes canary/A-B rollouts are built in—console shows token-level cost and quality delta if you feed eval prompts.
[06:29] [07:00] Ethan: security/compliance—SOC2 is a must, also data residency in EU. if we go Hosted, can you guarantee data stays in eu region?
[07:09] Samir: hosted infra has EU regions and we can pin workloads to eu-west. For strict residency and control, Redwood Private or Dedicated in your VPC is commonly used. we'll share SOC2 report and an architecture note.
[07:22] Luis: encryption keys—do we support customer-managed keys?
[07:26] Jordan: yes, KMS/HSM integrations for Private and Dedicated. For Hosted we support bring-your-own-key patterns in enterprise tiers.
[07:33] [07:55] Priya: operational visibility—we need per-route token cost and traceability for chargeback. does console provide that?
[07:59] Maya: maya here, CSM. yes the console exposes per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, traces and sample requests. retention is configurable.
[08:10] [08:30] Ana: about evals—we want to measure Spanish/Portuguese NDCG or BLEU? what are typical metrics you provide?
[08:38] Jordan: we provide perplexity, exact-match for structured outputs, NDCG for ranking tasks, and custom evals using your annotations. we'll run the Spanish/Portuguese corpus through each candidate model and produce a comparison sheet.
[08:51] [09:15] Priya: sample models—what are the top 3 you recommend for our profile (multilingual, 32k, tool-calling)?
[09:23] Jordan: candidate A: Mistral long-context variant (good latency/cost, fair multilingual), candidate B: Llama-derivative 70B-32k finetuned (better multilingual fidelity with tuning), candidate C: Open weights 100B long-context on Dedicated (best fidelity but highest infra cost).
[09:39] Ana: do these play well with function-calling?
[09:42] Jordan: yes function-calling is model-agnostic in redwood; output schema enforcement sits in the runtime and can reject/annotate noisy calls.
[09:50] [10:00] Ethan: what's the upgrade path from Hosted to Dedicated/Private? downtime? data migration?
[10:06] Samir: upgrade is mostly config and routing changes. You can route traffic gradually. For private deployments, there is a deployment window but we provide tooling to replicate model artifacts; we don't require data migration unless you move vectors or logs.
[10:17] Luis: if we host vectors on-prem, what about latency when hosted models need embeddings?
[10:23] Jordan: that's where colocated inference (private) helps. If hosted model calls your VPC vector store you can hit network tail. we recommend colocated Dedicated/Private for low-tail latency on retrieval-heavy flows.
[10:37] [11:00] Ana: can we try a PoC with mixed approach—hosted smaller model in prod flows and dedicated for 32k heavy flows?
[11:07] Samir: absolutely—hybrid routing is common. we'll sketch an architecture: hosted for most, dedicated for heavy flows, policy routing by endpoint.
[11:14] Priya: timeline—we'd like a pilot in 4 weeks. feasible?
[11:18] Jordan: feasible if we get prompt corpus and sample sessions this week. dedicated sizing needs infra info from luis.
[11:25] [12:00] Samir: let's talk benchmarks—Jordan will send a benchmark template. what payloads do you prefer?
[12:29] Ana: full chat logs anonymized, Spanish/Portuguese sets, and 50 catalog items for retrieval.
[12:35] Jordan: perfect. we'll request those via the onboarding doc.
[12:40] [13:00] Priya: other misc: vendor lock-in concerns. if we train finetunes, can we export artifacts?
[13:08] Samir: for Dedicated/Private you fully control model artifacts. For Hosted we offer export where permitted by model license; we'll clarify per-model.
[13:18] Ethan: any gotchas with open-weights license?
[13:21] Jordan: yes check model licenses (Llama successors, etc.). some open weights have commercial restrictions; our model catalog annotates licensing.
[13:30] [14:00] Ana: ok next steps recap?
[14:05] Samir: i'll recap: Samir send pricing and SOC2 by 6/5; Jordan send benchmark template and initial latency/cost projection by 6/7; BluePeak to provide sample corpus + infra constraints by 6/10; schedule sizing call week of 6/16.
[14:20] Priya: sounds good.
[14:23] Luis: thanks all.
[14:25] [End] Notes: a few stutters and small transcription errors; proper nouns like RedPajama and Mistral were occasionally mis-transcribed in the raw output.
